title: docs(workflows): document taskReadinessGate modes and gate classifications (T227)
body:
## Summary Operators selecting `ralphCodex.taskReadinessGate` (especially `strict`) previously got no guidance from the docs surface: `docs/workflows.md` described the modes only inline in **Planning Pass** and never enumerated which pre-execution decisions each mode can produce. This adds a dedicated, drift-guarded **Task Readiness Gate** section. (T227) What changed: - **`docs/workflows.md`** — new `## Task Readiness Gate` section that: - lists the six `PlanningGateDecision` classifications the gate emits — `proceed`, `warn_and_proceed`, `decomposed_and_stop`, `blocked_and_stop`, `human_review_and_stop`, `skipped`; - maps each mode (`off | warn | auto | strict`) to the subset it is allowed to emit, including `strict`'s extra executable-shape enforcement (validation + acceptance + bounded scope + planner `ready`); - links back to [Planning Pass](#planning-pass) / [Greenfield Readiness](#greenfield-readiness) and points the doc→code mapping at `src/ralph/planningGate.ts` (the module that actually evaluates the gate — `task.notes` guessed `preflight.ts`). - Describes behavior rather than restating the `package.json` enum description (per task constraint). - **`src/validation/docsValidator.ts`** — guard the section against drift: add `Task Readiness Gate` to the workflows `requiredHeadings` and `src/ralph/planningGate.ts` to `requiredFragments`. - **`test/docsValidator.test.ts`** — regression test asserting `missing_heading` + `missing_fragment` fire when the section/module reference is dropped; fixture updated so the valid baseline includes the new section. - **`AGENTS.md`** — extend the existing planning-pass pointer with a `taskReadinessGate` → `#task-readiness-gate` link (in-place to stay within the 105 non-empty-line budget). - **`out/validation/docsValidator.js(.map)`** — regenerated to stay in sync with `src/` (CI enforces `git diff --exit-code -- out/` excluding `out/webview-ui/`). No runtime `taskReadinessGate` behavior changed — docs + validator only. `npm run validate` passes (1424 tests, 0 fail); `npm run check:docs` passes. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/b9797888ec9a41c6a362ed704c15d0a3 Requested by: @S0l0m0n8und9

Greptile Summary

 This PR adds a dedicated **Task Readiness Gate** section to `docs/workflows.md`, enumerating the six `PlanningGateDecision` classifications and the subset each mode (`off | warn | auto | strict`) can emit. Drift-guards are wired in `src/validation/docsValidator.ts` and a regression test in `test/docsValidator.test.ts` confirms the guard fires when the heading or module reference is removed. - **`docs/workflows.md`** gains a new `## Task Readiness Gate` section that accurately reflects `src/ralph/planningGate.ts` behavior — gate modes, decision classifications, and cross-links to `#planning-pass` / `#greenfield-readiness` are all correct. - **`src/validation/docsValidator.ts`** adds `'Task Readiness Gate'` to `requiredHeadings` and `'src/ralph/planningGate.ts'` to `requiredFragments` for `docs/workflows.md`. - **`test/docsValidator.test.ts`** adds a negative test asserting `missing_heading` and `missing_fragment` fire when the section is dropped; the shared `seedValidRepository` fixture is updated with the minimal valid content. - **`AGENTS.md`** extends the planning-pass pointer with the new anchor; non-empty line count lands exactly at the 105-line budget.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Docs-and-validator-only change with no runtime behavior modified; all new content was cross-checked against planningGate.ts and is accurate. The new documentation section accurately reflects every decision branch in planningGate.ts — mode-to-classification mappings, fallback behavior, and the skipped conditions were all verified against the implementation. The drift guard and regression test are wired correctly, the AGENTS.md line budget is exactly met, the compiled out/ file matches the TypeScript source, and both anchor links in the new section resolve to real headings. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | docs/workflows.md | New ## Task Readiness Gate section accurately documents the six PlanningGateDecision outcomes and per-mode classifications; cross-links to #planning-pass and #greenfield-readiness are valid anchors. | | src/validation/docsValidator.ts | Adds 'Task Readiness Gate' to requiredHeadings and 'src/ralph/planningGate.ts' to requiredFragments for docs/workflows.md; both align with what the new section actually contains. | | test/docsValidator.test.ts | New test correctly seeds a fixture that omits the heading and module reference, then asserts both missing_heading and missing_fragment codes fire; the valid baseline fixture is updated to include the minimal required content. | | AGENTS.md | Inline addition of the taskReadinessGate → #task-readiness-gate link; non-empty line count is exactly 105, within budget. | | out/validation/docsValidator.js | Regenerated compiled output; 'Task Readiness Gate' and 'src/ralph/planningGate.ts' are present at the expected positions, consistent with the TypeScript source change. |

Flowchart

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[PlanningGate.evaluate] --> B{selectedTask?} B -- No --> SKIP[skipped] B -- Yes --> C{gateMode} C -- off + planning disabled --> SKIP C -- off + planning enabled --> D[load/run plan] D --> E{plan produced?} E -- No --> SKIP E -- Yes --> PROCEED[proceed] C -- warn --> F[load/run plan] F --> G{readiness != ready or findings?} G -- Yes --> WARN[warn_and_proceed] G -- No --> PROCEED2[proceed] C -- auto --> H[load/run plan] H --> I{block_or_review finding?} I -- Yes --> BLOCK[blocked_and_stop] I -- No --> J{needs_decomposition + valid children?} J -- Yes --> DECOMP[decomposed_and_stop] J -- No --> I2{blocked readiness?} I2 -- Yes --> BLOCK2[blocked_and_stop] I2 -- No --> J2{needs_human_review?} J2 -- Yes --> HR[human_review_and_stop] J2 -- No --> END[proceed / warn_and_proceed] C -- strict --> H2[load/run plan] H2 --> I3{block_or_review finding?} I3 -- Yes --> BLOCK3[blocked_and_stop] I3 -- No --> J3{needs_decomposition + valid children?} J3 -- Yes --> DECOMP2[decomposed_and_stop] J3 -- No --> K[assessStrictReadiness] K --> L{strict findings?} L -- Yes needs_human_review --> HR2[human_review_and_stop] L -- Yes other --> BLOCK4[blocked_and_stop] L -- No --> END2[proceed / warn_and_proceed] ```
